introduction: The paper presents a protocol for a systematic review with meta-analysis. It aims to guide a future review of the effects of aerobic exercise on reducing depression levels in adults.
methodology: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials in adults (>18 years) with depression, following PRISMA-P and registered in PROSPERO. The search will cover BVS, Cochrane Library, Embase, Epistemonikos, PubMed and SPORTDiscus, with no restriction on date or language. Two reviewers will select studies independently, and a third reviewer will decide disagreements. Risk of bias will use TESTEX and RoB 2.0; certainty will be rated with GRADE.
discussion: The authors say aerobic exercise has been shown to be a potential depression treatment, comparable to various therapeutic approaches, including medication, psychotherapy and other exercise-based therapies. They expect high heterogeneity among the studies to be included.
limitations: The authors anticipate small sample sizes, unclear mechanisms, varied intensity protocols and high heterogeneity among included studies as challenges for the future review.

introduction.q: This protocol proposal aims to guide a future systematic review that will seek to answer the following question: what are the effects of aerobic exercise on reducing depression levels in adults?

methodology.q: The study is a protocol for a systematic review, which will follow the guidelines developed by Page et al.
registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews - PROSPERO, number: CRD42024592700
Participants will include adults (>18 years) diagnosed with depression
Eligible study types will be randomized clinical trials (RCTs), no restriction of language
The intervention will focus on aerobic exercise (e.g., walking, running), with comparators including other interventions or control groups.
The primary outcome will be depressive symptoms
The search will be conducted in the following databases: BVS, Cochrane library, Embase, Epistemonikos, PubMed and SPORTDiscus.
There will be no restrictions on publication date or language.
Studies will be selected independently by two researchers using the Rayyan ‘QCRI’ software.
A third senior and expert reviewer (I.K.S) will review any articles in case of disagreement
The methodological quality assessment of the included studies will be carried out by two independent reviewers (L.N.S; M.I.K) using the TESTEX tool
the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool (RoB 2.0) will be used to assess the risk of bias in the included studies
The meta-analysis will be conducted using fixed-effect or random-effects models, depending on the heterogeneity among the included studies.
RevMan version 5.3.5 will be used for all analyses, including meta-analysis if feasible

discussion.q: Aerobic exercise has been shown to be a potential strategy for treating depression in different populations, being comparable to various therapeutic approaches, including medication, psychotherapy, and other exercise-based therapies.
one of the main methodological challenges expected in the conduction of this review is the high heterogeneity among the studies to be included

limitations.q: Anticipated limitations and challenges include the following issues: the use of small sample sizes, lack of clarity regarding the specific mechanisms through which exercise contributes to the improvement of depression, and variations in the intensity protocols adopted.

abstract_claims.q: Studies suggest that aerobic exercise can improve mental health and reduce depression symptoms, despite variations in exercise type and intensity.

It is expected that the systematic review following this protocol will identify the effective dose-response to reduce depression levels and provide an understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression.

caveats.q: Although the benefits of aerobic exercise in improving depressive symptoms are well documented, the existing literature shows high variability in terms of modality, intensity, frequency, and duration of exercise.
Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms of these effects are still not fully understood
However, many existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses have methodological limitations that prevent definitive conclusions.

However, the findings did not allow for the precise establishment of a dose-response relationship due to variability in the study protocols analyzed, particularly regarding frequency, duration, and weekly volume of activity
However, the analysis of these exercises should not be based solely on perceived effort or heart rate

An analysis of exercise intensity in studies indicated that although more intense activities may offer additional benefits, the potential gains for reducing depressive symptoms are not limited to high-intensity levels.
Given the gaps in the literature that have yet to establish an optimal dose-response of physical exercise in the management of depression
Although exercise is not yet considered an essential component on its own
The systematic review studies conducted so far, although following rigorous methodologies and providing relevant contributions to the scientific field, present some methodological limitations.
In addition, one of the main methodological challenges expected in the conduction of this review is the high heterogeneity among the studies to be included.

Anticipated limitations and challenges include the following issues: the use of small sample sizes, lack of clarity regarding the specific mechanisms through which exercise contributes to the improvement of depression, and variations in the intensity protocols adopted.
Only studies utilizing validated depression assessment scales will be included
excluding individuals with chronic degenerative diseases or other associated severe psychiatric disorders
ongoing clinical trials with preliminary results will be excluded

studies involving populations with non-communicable chronic diseases (e.g., hypertension, diabetes), case reports, preprints, narrative and systematic reviews, and observational studies will not be considered for inclusion
a funnel plot, which will be generated only if at least 10 studies are included in the meta-analysis
excluding blinding domains due to the nature of physical exercise interventions
